title: Post-Deployment Drift Monitor: A Simple Tool for Tracking Safety Score Changes Over Time
original_idea: Build a lightweight Python tool that periodically runs a fixed set of AILuminate-style safety probes against a local model endpoint and logs scores over time, flagging statistically significant drops. Validate by intentionally fine-tuning a model to degrade safety and confirming the tool detects it.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Post-deployment monitoring is identified as a critical gap by the 2026 safety report. Directly addresses an acknowledged need.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a Python monitoring tool is feasible for CS students. The validation step (fine-tuning a model to degrade safety) adds significant complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tool building plus validation via fine-tuning is two distinct projects. The tool alone is narrow; the validation broadens scope.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple production-grade LLM monitoring tools already exist in 2026: Confident AI (50+ metrics including safety), Langfuse, Arize AI, Helicone, and LangSmith all provide drift detection, safety monitoring, and alerting. Automated drift detection services track validator compliance, length drift, semantic similarity, and regression. Quality-aware alerting on faithfulness, relevance, safety, and latency is standard in production tooling. The proposed lightweight Python tool is a simplified version of existing commercial and open-source solutions. The validation via intentional fine-tuning is a more novel component but does not offset the overall coverage.
